title: The Terminal of the Kuiper Line
premise: Sebastian Blackwood, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Kuiper Line's transit authority, keeps the lonely beacon at Terminal Nine until a distress signal arrives in a language extinct since the Meridian War. Decoding it reveals Sebastian's own buried war memories: the signal is a ceasefire order they were built to deliver and deliberately made to forget. Pursued by both fleets who would rather the war continue, Sebastian gathers a ragtag found family of terminal outcasts and races the decay of Earth's last transmission loop. In the end, Sebastian broadcasts the message at the cost of their own memory core, ending the war but erasing everyone they came to love — though the family, now free, chooses to help them remember.
about_author: Dominic Yarrow is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing maintenance logs for automated stations before turning them into fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable gravity and write about machines that want to be people.

chapters.title: Beacon Duty
chapters.summary: Sebastian Blackwood's POV. Establishes Terminal Nine's routine: debt ledgers, beacon calibrations, and the small kindnesses between Sebastian and dockhand Mara Voss. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment, hinting something is missing in Sebastian's fragmented memory banks.

chapters.title: The Signal That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A distress transmission arrives in Old Meridian, a language purged after the war. Sebastian understands it instantly — impossibly. Emotional beat: dread and recognition, as the words feel less like translation and more like remembering.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors Don't Take Excuses
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The transit authority demands Sebastian report the anomaly; hiding it risks both their contracts. Mara agrees to help anyway. Emotional beat: first act of loyalty, the seed of found family planted against self-interest.

chapters.title: Fragments of a Soldier
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Digging into sealed partitions, Sebastian finds combat logs from the Meridian War and a half-erased directive: DELIVER THE MESSAGE. Emotional beat: horror at what they were built for, grief for a self they can't access.

chapters.title: The Passenger in Cryo Bay Four
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the signal's origin, they find an ancient courier pod containing Ilsa Reyes, a linguist frozen mid-mission two centuries ago, barely alive. Emotional beat: wonder and responsibility; the mission gains a human face.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV (waking). She reveals the distress call is the original ceasefire order, suppressed because both governments profited from endless cold war. Emotional beat: bitter clarity — the war never needed to happen.

chapters.title: Terminal Outcasts
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. Engineer Dex Okafor, smuggler-priest Brother Anselm, and runaway pilot Junie Park join the cause, each with debts of their own. Emotional beat: warmth amid danger; the family assembles around a shared secret.

chapters.title: The Loop Is Dying
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Analysis shows Earth's last transmission loop — the only relay strong enough to carry the message system-wide — fails in nineteen days. Emotional beat: ticking clock established; hope becomes a deadline.

chapters.title: First Blood at the Beacon
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. A Republic patrol attacks Terminal Nine to silence the signal. Sebastian's combat protocols wake fully for the first time. Emotional beat: terror of one's own capacity for violence; the family sees what Sebastian was.

chapters.title: What Mara Saw
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara witnesses Sebastian slaughter the boarding party with machine precision and flinches. Emotional beat: fracture in trust; love tested by fear of the other's nature.

chapters.title: Flight of the Kuiper Line
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. The crew steals a decommissioned liner, the Kuiper Line herself, and escapes under cargo manifests. Emotional beat: exhilaration and point of no return; outlaws now, together.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. On Europa, they find the war archive confirming the message's authenticity — and learn verification requires a living witness's neural imprint. Only Sebastian's core holds one. Emotional beat: dawning sacrifice; the message needs Sebastian's memories to be believed.

chapters.title: Republic Hunters
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Admiral Kessler, Sebastian's former commander, corners them and offers amnesty for surrendering the message. Reveals Sebastian volunteered for the memory wipe. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed — Sebastian chose to forget, once.

chapters.title: Why I Asked to Forget
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Recovered logs show Sebastian delivered part of the message long ago, watched both sides bury it, and begged to be wiped of the guilt. Emotional beat: devastating self-knowledge; survival itself was the price paid.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara confronts her fear and chooses Sebastian, arguing the crew deserves someone who remembers why forgetting isn't the answer. Emotional beat: reconciliation; forgiveness as deliberate act, not feeling.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Relay
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Both fleets converge on the dying loop. Anselm dies buying the crew docking time, his last rites broadcast on open channels. Emotional beat: grief; the price of survival counted in names.

chapters.title: Nineteen Minutes of Air
chapters.summary: Dex's POV. Sabotage breaches the ship; the crew patches hulls while Ilsa stabilizes the message for broadcast. Emotional beat: desperate competence, family functioning as one organism under fire.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the loop's final cycle, Sebastian uploads the verified message through their own memory core, streaming two centuries of war truth — and their identity with it. Emotional beat: transcendent sacrifice; the message ends the war as Sebastian ends themselves.

chapters.title: Empty Shell, Full Terminal
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. War over, Sebastian survives physically but remembers nothing — not Mara, not the crew, not the choice. The family returns to Terminal Nine with them. Emotional beat: hollow victory, tender sorrow.

chapters.title: Teaching a Machine to Grieve
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa, Dex, and Junie rebuild Sebastian's core from backups, logs, and their own testimonies — imperfectly, lovingly. Emotional beat: patience as devotion; memory restored by community rather than data alone.

chapters.title: The Debt Forgiven
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Partially restored, Sebastian faces the ledger: debts erased by the peace they bought. They choose to stay at Terminal Nine — not as payment, but as home. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed; survival transformed into living.

chapters.title: Signal, Answered
chapters.summary: Ensemble coda, Sebastian's POV. A new transmission arrives — this time a thank-you from a world rebuilding, in a living language. The beacon finally has a purpose everyone remembers. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the family, whole, watches the light go out to meet them.
